reason: This is a careful plan for a runner coming back from a stress reaction. It keeps the physio's limit of walk-runs three days a week (Mon, Wed, Sat), and each one is short (14 to 15 minutes, 1-minute run rounds) on flat routes. There's a rest day after each run. The only step up is to 1.5-minute rounds on Saturday, and that only goes ahead if the shin stays quiet. That's a sensible pace toward the mid-October goal of 30 minutes nonstop, so she isn't being rushed. The physio calf and hip routine is kept on Tue and Fri, and the safety flag tells her to check in with the physio if the shin changes. Each day is clear enough to run as written. I took a point off because the draft states "0/10 pain and effort 3/10" for every run, and the card doesn't give those numbers. It only says "shin quiet" and "nervous but happy." That detail looks invented. The visible text also does little with her nervousness beyond reassuring her that the week went cleanly.

Ines ran about 40 km a week before a stress reaction in the left shin and ten weeks off, and a physio has cleared Ines for walk-run three days a week, stopping if the shin aches. The goal is to run 30 minutes without walking by mid-October.
Recent weeks: none recorded.
This week: 5.1 km over 3 runs.
Body: "Shin quiet."
Feeling: "Nervous but happy to be back."
